cards.text: Ruth, a widow from Moab, lives with her mother-in-law, Naomi. One day Naomi opens with "My daughter," and friend, when a talk starts like that, you put the dough DOWN. Naomi's got something on her mind for Ruth.

cards.question: Naomi says she wants to seek something for Ruth, so that it may be well with her. What is it?

cards.text: Then Naomi brings up Boaz, the man whose servant girls Ruth has been working with. And Naomi isn't just bringing him up. She knows his SCHEDULE.

cards.question: Naomi reminds Ruth that Boaz is a ___ of theirs.
Naomi knows where Boaz will be tonight, winnowing barley. Where is he?

cards.text: Now Naomi gets ready to send Ruth out. And this plan comes with a getting-ready list.

cards.question: Naomi tells Ruth to head to the threshing floor just as she is, in her work clothes.

cards.text: Wash, perfume, best clothes. Me? I've worn this same apron since the day I got here, and I call THAT dressing up.

cards.question: Naomi says the timing matters. When can Ruth let Boaz know she's there?

answers.text: After he finishes eating and drinking
As soon as she gets there

cards.text: Then Naomi gets to the part for after Boaz lies down. Ruth is supposed to note the place where he lies.

cards.question: Then Ruth is supposed to go in, uncover his ___, and lie down.
Naomi says Boaz will explain to Ruth what she should do.

cards.text: That is a LOT of plan, friend. Hand me that and I've got nine questions, a notepad and a nervous sweat.

cards.question: How does Ruth answer Naomi's plan?

answers.text: I will do everything you say
Let me think it over first

cards.text: So Ruth goes down to the threshing floor and does everything Naomi told her. Boaz finishes eating and drinking, he's in good spirits, and he lies down at the end of the heap of grain.

cards.question: Ruth marches in and announces herself to Boaz.

cards.text: At midnight, Boaz is startled, turns over, and there's a woman lying at his feet! I'd have jumped clean off my gold base, friend, and I'm ATTACHED to it.

cards.question: Boaz asks who she is, and Ruth tells him. Then what does Ruth ask Boaz to do?

answers.text: Spread the corner of his garment over her
Walk her home to Naomi at first light
Speak to the elders of the town for her

cards.question: What reason does Ruth give Boaz for asking?

answers.text: He is a man of the LORD

cards.text: Now, Boaz just got startled awake at midnight. I get grumpy when my oven timer goes off, but Boaz says, "May the LORD bless you, my daughter."

cards.question: Boaz tells Ruth she has shown more kindness now than before.
Boaz says Ruth has not run after the ___ men, whether rich or poor.

cards.text: Then Boaz tells her not to be afraid. He'll do for her whatever she asks.

cards.question: Boaz says all his fellow townspeople know Ruth is a woman of noble ___.

cards.text: Then Boaz says, "Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but…" Oh no, friend. There is a BUT.

cards.question: Boaz says no redeemer is nearer to Ruth than he is.

cards.text: So Boaz lays out the plan. Ruth stays tonight, and in the morning, if the nearer redeemer wants to redeem her, good, let him.

cards.question: And if the nearer redeemer doesn't want to? What does Boaz promise, as surely as the LORD lives?

answers.text: He will send her back to Moab

cards.text: So Ruth lies at his feet until morning. She gets up before anyone else could recognize her.

cards.question: Boaz wants word to get around that a woman came to the threshing floor.

cards.text: Then Boaz tells Ruth to bring the shawl she's wearing and hold it out. Look at this man, packing a shawl like I pack a cookie box, except he's using his HANDS like some kind of amateur.

cards.question: Boaz pours ___ measures of barley into Ruth's shawl and places it on her.

cards.text: Boaz heads into the city, and Ruth heads home to Naomi, who asks, "How did it go, my daughter?" Ruth tells her everything Boaz did for her.

cards.question: What does Ruth say Boaz told her when he gave her the barley?

answers.text: Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed
Bring this to your mother-in-law before sunrise
Share this grain with the servant girls tomorrow

cards.question: Naomi tells Ruth to wait until she finds out how things go. Why?

answers.text: Boaz will not rest until it is settled today
The nearer redeemer is away from town
Boaz needs some time to think it over

cards.text: And that's where Naomi leaves it, friend. I spent years waiting in a junk drawer, so believe me when I tell you this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card says Ruth is a widow from Moab, which comes from Ruth 1, not Ruth 3:1. The card cites only Ruth 3:1, so this outside fact appears without its reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Story card 6 says the plan 'comes with a getting-ready list.' That rules out 'just as she is, in her work clothes' before the baker answers, so the true or false on card 7 is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the size of Naomi's plan. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward, even though it cites Ruth 3:4.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke 'I'd have jumped clean off my gold base' depends on Papa Dorin leaving his base. Even as a joke, this breaks the character rule that the base always comes with him.

rule.text: He can hop, jump and dive face-first into the chocolate chips, but the base always comes with him. He never steps off it or leaves it behind.

findings.problem: The card retells Boaz being startled at midnight (Ruth 3:8) but cites only Ruth 3:10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke calls Boaz 'some kind of amateur' for using his hands. That laughs at a person in the Bible story instead of with his situation, and the joke isn't on Papa Dorin himself.

rule.text: When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: The card has three things happening: Boaz goes into the city, Ruth returns and Naomi asks how it went, and Ruth tells her everything Boaz did.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
